Si vous n'avez pas toutes les qualifications requises mais que ce poste vous intéresse, postulez sans hésiter. Poste basé à Wasquehal. En tant que Comptable Fournisseurs Senior, vous jouerez un rôle clé dans la fiabilité des comptes fournisseurs et l'optimisation des processus financiers. Gestion des factures fournisseurs Contrôler et enregistrer les factures fournisseurs dans le respect des normes comptables, fiscales et légales. Effectuer le rapprochement des factures avec les bons de commande et les réceptions de marchandises ou services. Vérifier la conformité des taxes, du prix et des termes de paiement. Identifier, analyser et résoudre les écarts ou litiges de facturation en collaboration avec les fournisseurs et les équipes internes. Gestion de la relation fournisseurs Assurer une communication régulière avec les fournisseurs pour le suivi des demandes et la résolution des problématiques. Contribuer au maintien de relations de qualité avec les partenaires externes. Gestion des paiements Participer à la préparation des campagnes de paiement. Veiller au respect des échéances de règlement et garantir l'exactitude des paiements effectués. Contrôle et clôture comptable Garantir la correcte comptabilisation des opérations fournisseurs et leur réconciliation avec le grand livre. Analyser et justifier les comptes fournisseurs, notamment les balances âgées. Participer activement aux clôtures mensuelles et préparer les écritures d'ajustement nécessaires (charges à payer, provisions, factures non parvenues, etc.). Reporting, audit et amélioration continue Préparer les documents et analyses requis dans le cadre des audits internes et externes. Accompagner et soutenir les comptables fournisseurs sur les processus quotidiens et les bonnes pratiques comptables. Participer aux projets d'amélioration continue visant à renforcer l'efficacité des processus, des outils et de l'organisation. Requirements 8 à 10 ans d’expérience en comptabilité fournisseurs, idéalement dans un environnement international et/ou multisites. Solide maîtrise des processus Procure-to-Pay (P2P), des principes comptables et des contrôles associés. Excellente maîtrise des outils ERP (SAP Public Cloud, Business Central) et Excel. Bonnes capacités d’analyse, de résolution de problèmes et de réconciliation comptable. Aisance relationnelle et capacité à collaborer efficacement avec les fournisseurs et les parties prenantes internes. Sensibilité à l’amélioration continue et à l’automatisation des processus, avec une volonté de contribuer à la transformation de la fonction finance. Meet Arago and the Aragonians

Arago is an AI and computer hardware company whose mission is to drive the course of history forward. We do so by accelerating breakthroughs at the intersection of AI and semiconductors.

Founded in 2024 by AI researchers and physicists with deep expertise in photonics, electronics, software, mathematics, and machine learning, Arago brings together a lean team of engineers and scientists from the world’s top companies and research labs.

Composed of nine nationalities and operating from hubs in France, North America, and Israel, we believe in great science and fast achievements. Our work is guided by these core principles:

  1. Do great things: we deliver work we’re proud to sign our name to.

  2. High velocity: speed matters. We move quickly, one step at a time.

  3. One unit: we’re all in this together, with relationships grounded in trust, respect, and camaraderie.

Arago is backed by executives from Apple, Arm, Nvidia, Microsoft, and Hugging Face, as well as prominent US and European deeptech venture firms and exited founders.

What you’ll do

As a Drivers & Virtualization Engineer, you will own the host-facing software boundary of Arago’s accelerator. Your mission is to ensure our hardware is accessible, secure, and performant across diverse environments—ranging from bare-metal deployments to complex virtualized and multi-device cloud infrastructures. You will focus on building robust kernel-level interfaces where correctness, isolation, and long-term operational safety are paramount.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

  • Deep knowledge of OS internals, particularly kernel memory management and I/O paths.

  • Strong understanding of memory safety requirements in kernel space.

  • Proven hands-on experience in Linux kernel driver development and kernel modules.

  • Solid understanding of virtualization fundamentals (KVM, hypervisors).

  • Practical experience with emulation frameworks, specifically QEMU internals or custom device models.

  • Familiarity with hardware-level protocols: PCIe, DMA, MMIO, and IOMMU.

  • Language: English at a proficient level. French is a plus.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain high-performance Linux kernel drivers for Arago’s proprietary accelerator.

  • Implement communication protocols and virtual device interfaces to bridge hardware and software.

  • Manage low-level hardware interactions including PCIe, DMA, MMIO, and interrupt handling.

  • Enable seamless virtualized access to accelerators using QEMU and KVM.

  • Design and implement robust device sharing, passthrough, and isolation mechanisms.

  • Ensure the security of accelerator operations through strict memory protection and resource isolation.

  • Debug complex failures that span the entire stack: from hardware and kernel to hypervisor and guest OS.

  • Support the scaling of our architecture from single-device setups to large-scale multi-device deployments.

Run acceptance tests against the agreed performance criteria and secure formal customer sign-off. A track record of delivering complex on-site projects end to end with real customer and budget accountability. Good understanding of warehouse operations and technical environments. Strong command of project management methods and tools: planning, risk management, budget tracking and reporting. Organized, rigorous and hands-on, you are comfortable spending a lot of time on site. Fluent French and English, you are willing to travel frequently across Europe. Nice to have: experience with AMR/AGV or palletization deployments, knowledge of WMS/WCS, site safety training. Piloter la préparation du site, l’installation, la mise en service et la montée en cadence. Mener les tests de réception selon les critères de performance contractuels, et obtenir la validation formelle du client. Assurer la passation à Run & Support avec une documentation complète : configuration, points ouverts, SLA et contacts. Senior ML Manager - Applied AI & Voice (x/f/m)

Set a new pulse for healthcare!

We are looking for a Senior ML Manager to join the Voice team in our Applied AI organization.

Your mission will be to drive the development of AI-powered voice and language technologies that meaningfully reduce administrative burden for healthcare professionals and improve the quality of patient care. You will lead engineering teams building state-of-the-art speech recognition and conversational AI products — including real-time transcription, clinical dictation, and phone assistance — contributing directly to better healthcare experiences for millions of patients and practitioners every day.

Working in the tech team at Doctolib means building innovative products and features to improve the daily lives of care teams and patients.

 

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead and develop two ML engineering teams (8 engineers), owning performance management, career development, and talent retention to build a high-performing, impact-driven culture

  • Own the technical direction of your perimeter, including architecture choices and trade-offs, ensuring teams build the right things the right way across the ASR product scope

  • Define and drive the roadmap for your teams in alignment with organizational OKRs, navigating ambiguity and making fast, informed decisions in an evolving environment

  • Act as a technical promoter for your teams, maintaining full visibility across all engineering domains, deeply understanding system design constraints, and challenging technical decisions with confidence

  • Partner with Talent & People as Hiring Manager to attract and recruit top ML engineering talent, and champion a culture of high standards and fast execution

  • Contribute to broader Applied AI initiatives as a senior engineering leader, identifying synergies across teams and ensuring technical coherence across the voice and ASR perimeter

 

Who you are

Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Have 3+ years of people management experience leading ML or Data Science engineering teams

  • Have a strong technical background in Machine Learning (classical ML is a must), with the ability to understand, challenge, and make architectural decisions on complex ML systems at a level benchmarked against leading industry standards

  • Have deep understanding of system design, trade-offs, and technical risk management, allowing you to guide your teams effectively without blind spots

  • Are comfortable operating across multiple technical domains simultaneously, thriving in environments with fast decisions, ambiguity, and frequent scope changes

  • Are fluent in English; French is a plus

It would be fantastic if you:

  • Have hands-on experience with ASR, speech processing, or audio ML

  • Are familiar with LLMs and their integration into production ML systems

  • Have experience managing multi-team organisations or acting as a manager of managers

 

Life at Doctolib Tech

  • Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to country and healthcare specialty requirements.

  • Our stack is composed of Rails, TypeScript, Java, Python, Kotlin, Swift, and React Native.

  • We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here.

Want to learn more about our tech culture and environment? Visit the Doctolib Tech site.

 

What we offer

  • Free comprehensive health insurance (basic package) for you and your children

  • 25 days of paid vacation per year, plus up to 14 days of RTT

  • Free mental health and coaching services through our partner Moka.care

  • Work from abroad for up to 10 days per year thanks to our flexibility days policy

  • Lunch vouchers (Swile card) worth €8.50 per working day, with €4.50 covered by Doctolib

  • A subsidy from the work council to refund part of the membership to a sport club or a creative class

  • 50% reimbursement of your public transport subscription

  • ParentCare Program: Enjoy full salary coverage (100%) during your first month of birth leave and 75% during the second, covered by Doctolib

  • Enrollment in Doctolib's long-term employee value sharing plan called DoctoGrowth

  • For caregivers and workers with disabilities, a package including an adaptation of the remote policy, extra days off for medical reasons, and psychological support

  • Relocation support in case of international mobility

  • Access to the best AI tools for coding, development and dedicated training

 

Our interview process

  • Recruiter Call (45 min)

  • Hiring Manager Interview — in-depth discussion on people management approach and leadership experience (30 min)

  • System Design Interview — assess architectural thinking and ability to challenge complex ML systems (1h)

  • Behavioral Interview — assess leadership, decision-making in ambiguity, and management philosophy (1h)

  • Meet the team (45 min)

  • Leadership Interview (30 min)

  • At least one reference check

We want your experience to be clear, respectful, and transparent. Learn more about our hiring process on our candidate experience page.

 

Job details

  • Permanent position

  • Full-time

  • Location: Doctolib Paris office, Levallois-Perret

  • Hybrid work setup (up to 2 remote days per week)

  • Start date: as soon as possible

 

We welcome everyone

At Doctolib, we are committed to improving access to healthcare for everyone. This translates into our recruitment process. We evaluate candidates based solely on qualifications and motivation, without any form of discrimination.

The more diverse ideas are heard, the more our product will truly improve healthcare for all. You are welcome to apply to Doctolib, regardless of your gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, or disability.

To ensure equal opportunities, we invite you to exclude personal information (e.g., pictures, age) from your applications. If you require any accommodation, please let us know for support during the hiring process.

Join us in building the healthcare we all dream of!

title: Tritium Process Engineers
company: Personal data collected as part of the application process
description: About Tritium Fuel Cycle (TFC) GFG is designing a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) fusion power plant (FPP) to deliver 1 GW of electrical power in the 2040s. The “GIGA” plant will be based on a stellarator magnetic confinement fusion device, operating continuously on a deuterium-tritium (D-T) fuel cycle. Prior to this, the smaller “Gauss Industrial Demonstrator (GID-170)” will be deployed in the mid-2030s. While deuterium can be extracted from seawater, tritium is a tightly controlled radioactive isotope with an extremely limited global supply. Therefore, both GID-170 and GIGA must utilise closed tritium fuel cycle infrastructure, to ensure that unburnt tritium is fully recycled back to the stellarator and not released to the environment. Meanwhile, the tritium consumed by the fusion reaction must be replenished using tritium breeding blankets (TBB). A first-of-a-kind dedicated tritium fuel cycle (TFC) facility, suitable for continuously supporting a stellarator device, must be designed, built and commissioned. It will adopt a multi-loop process architecture, each loop comprising many deeply integrated subsystems. Developing such a facility presents unique engineering challenges: the supply chain is still emerging, commercial process simulation tools lack dedicated TFC libraries, suitable off-the-shelf equipment is not always available, and some technologies have relatively low technology readiness levels (TRLs). A conceptual design is currently under development, with the project then progressing into pre-front-end engineering design (pre-FEED) in 2028, followed by front-end engineering design (FEED) and design for manufacturing phases. Completion of the overall design phase (for GID-170) must be achieved by 2032. About the role GFG is looking for several Tritium Process Engineers to join the TFC department and develop the GID-170 and GIGA TFC facilities. The roles will contribute to the continued development and optimisation of the overall fuel cycle architecture and its subsystems. Activities will include managing design requirements; developing process flow diagrams (PFDs), piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), heat and mass balances (HMBs) and the Basis of Design (BoD); selecting technologies; sizing and arranging equipment; and contributing to safety-related design. The roles may also involve supporting equipment prototype development and testing with technology developers and research partners. We welcome candidates with complementary strengths in process design and process modelling and simulation, with systems engineering experience also desirable. These specialisations sit within the same engineering function, and candidates are not expected to have equal expertise across all areas. The number of appointments and balance of responsibilities will reflect the successful candidates’ experience and technical strengths. Drawing on their specialist expertise, successful candidates will work collaboratively on design development, modelling, analysis and optimisation to assess design alternatives and inform robust, well-documented design decisions. The TFC comprises a wide range of technologies and subsystems, requiring the department to manage multiple sub-projects and work packages in parallel. Each engineer will contribute across several activities and will be expected to take ownership of specific tasks or subsystems, or lead work packages, depending on their experience. The roles will involve close collaboration with engineers from the same and other disciplines at national and international partner organisations, research institutions and suppliers, as well as with colleagues across disciplines and departments within GFG. Given the specific challenges associated with tritium, close collaboration with Nuclear Safety and Export Control specialists will also be essential. During conceptual design, successful candidates will work closely with the Head of Tritium Fuel Cycle to address the strong interdependencies between subsystems and develop a coherent, integrated design. As the project moves into pre-FEED, they will be expected to take greater day-to-day ownership of their assigned areas and drive design development through pre-FEED and FEED, while maintaining close coordination across subsystem interfaces. As the project progresses, the roles will evolve to support design for manufacture, procurement and commissioning of the GID-170 TFC systems, followed by further development and refinement of the TFC design for GIGA. Main responsibilities Process definition and systems engineering Identify, define and manage system requirements and interfaces across TFC subsystems and the overall plant architecture. Develop and optimise the fuel cycle architecture, assessing alternative subsystem technologies, their respective advantages and disadvantages, technology readiness levels (TRLs), and potential system configurations. Develop process flow diagrams (PFDs) for individual TFC subsystem blocks and the overall plant architecture. Participate in the development of piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), identification and sizing of key components, and equipment layout. Develop and maintain representative heat and mass balances to support process definition, system integration and design decisions. Process modelling and simulation Develop, apply and improve process simulation models for individual TFC subsystem blocks and the overall plant architecture, using tools such as Aspen Plus, Aspen Custom Modeler, Python and dedicated proprietary software, as appropriate. Support the development and integration of custom models and, where appropriate, contribute to the development of dedicated simulation tools. Use modelling and simulation to assess system performance, compare technology options and operating configurations, support component sizing, and inform process optimisation and design decisions. Documentation of assumptions, uncertainty and applicability limits, and perform model validation when suitable data becomes available. Work collaboratively with internal and external modelling specialists to ensure consistency between simulation results, engineering requirements and the evolving plant design. Cost, safety and risk management Identify and manage design risks, developing effective risk-reduction strategies and action plans. Identify applicable standards, regulations and codes, and ensure that these are considered throughout the design process. Participate in hazard, safety and accident analyses, including hazard identification (HAZID) and hazard and operability (HAZOP) studies, and contribute to the definition of safety functions and development of the safety case. Contribute to capital and operational expenditure (CAPEX/OPEX) estimates. Design development and delivery Develop design documentation and specifications, including contributions to the Basis of Design and design philosophies. Document design studies, verification and assessment activities, engineering assumptions and design decisions. Support the design development, procurement and testing of prototypes for key components, in collaboration with technology developers, suppliers and research partners. Provide engineering support for R&D activities conducted in-house and with external partners and collaborators. Project coordination and collaboration Lead specific technical tasks or work packages assigned by the Head of TFC, in line with experience and expertise. Take ownership of specific subsystems throughout the pre-FEED and FEED studies, as assigned by the Head of TFC, in line with experience and expertise. Participate in technical meetings with partners, suppliers, research institutions and other collaborators. Collaborate closely with other engineering disciplines and contribute to the integration of TFC systems within the wider fusion plant. As required, undertake other relevant duties in support of project objectives. GID-170 delivery (in the 2030s) Support the procurement and installation activities of the GID-170 TFC facilities. Develop commissioning plans and operating instructions. The balance between process design, systems engineering, and process modelling and simulation will depend on each candidate’s background and area of expertise. All engineers are expected to work collaboratively across these areas, ensuring that modelling activities inform engineering decisions and that process design is supported by robust analysis. Qualification and educational requirements Required qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in chemical engineering, process engineering, nuclear engineering, or a closely related discipline*. *In the case of a closely related discipline, the degree should be supported by relevant chemical engineering experience. A minimum of 3 years design experience working as a Process Engineer in an industrial environment. Additional desirable qualifications relevant to process modelling and simulation : A PhD or EngD in Chemical or Process Engineering or a closely related field. Competences and preferred skills 1. Common skills Essential All applicants should demonstrate: In-depth knowledge of chemical engineering principles, including thermodynamics, heat and mass transfer, process dynamics, and relevant transport phenomena. Experience in the development of industrial-scale process engineering installations in complex environments requiring regulatory approval (ideally nuclear projects or similar). Experience in the development of processes involving different fluids and conditions (cryogenic, vacuum, atmospheric pressure gas, high-pressure gas (up to 100 bara), liquid, etc.). Experience in the design and development of integrated treatment unit operations (purification, separation, conditioning, etc.), ideally in the gas phase, and in the hydrogen or nuclear sectors. Proficiency in at least one established process simulation tool, such as Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, UniSim, gPROMS, ProMax, CHEMCAD or equivalent. Experience in requirements capture, documentation and management. Experience working alongside multiple other engineering disciplines, such as mechanical, electrical, control, thermal and nuclear engineers. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams of engineers, technologists and physicists. A proactive and self-motivated approach, with strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills. Professional working proficiency in English. Desirable All applicants would benefit from demonstrating: Knowledge of tritium fuel cycle technologies and/or hydrogen isotope separation. Hands-on experience working with tritium would be an advantage. Experience with the design or analysis of pumping technologies, heat exchangers or other key process equipment. Familiarity with magnetic fusion systems and/or nuclear power plant systems. Familiarity with environmental, nuclear safety and other relevant regulatory requirements. Knowledge of systems engineering and an understanding of configuration management and risk management. Understanding of equipment qualification, manufacture, testing, inspection and pragmatic usability. Knowledge of German or other European languages. 2. Specialist Skills Candidates are expected to demonstrate strengths in one or more of the following areas, depending on their background and specialisation. Process design and systems engineering Experience in developing process architectures, heat and mass balances, PFDs and P&IDs, and in supporting equipment selection, sizing and integration. Experience in developing Basis of Design (BoD) documentation, design philosophies, specifications, design descriptions and justifications. Ability to assess alternative process technologies and configurations, considering performance, safety, technical maturity and operational requirements. Experience in translating system requirements and process analysis into engineering specifications and design decisions. Familiarity with process safety codes, standards and regulations, as well as safety-by-design principles, including the ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) approach. Experience in engaging with potential technology suppliers and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). Process modelling and simulation Proficiency in process modelling tools such as Aspen Custom Modeler, gPROMS custom modelling or equivalent. Proficiency in at least one programming or scientific computing language, such as Python, Julia, MATLAB, Octave or C++. Strong understanding of numerical methods applied to chemical engineering, including ordinary and partial differential equations (ODEs and PDEs), differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), discretisation techniques and numerical convergence. Knowledge of numerical optimisation methods and their implementation, with the ability to apply them to process analysis and design optimisation. Experience developing custom process models, integrating subsystem models or analysing dynamic process behaviour, along with model automation and analysis, to assess system performance, compare design options and support process optimisation is an advantage. We are recruiting engineers with complementary technical strengths. Applicants who meet the common essential criteria and have relevant capability in one specialist profile are encouraged to apply; experience in every technology or software package listed is not expected. The balance of responsibilities and the level of technical ownership will be agreed according to each successful candidate’s experience and the needs of the programme, with opportunities for candidates to grow and develop into greater technical ownership.     4. Documentation of assumptions, uncertainty and applicability limits, and perform model validation when suitable data becomes available.
    5. Work collaboratively with internal and external modelling specialists to ensure consistency between simulation results, engineering requirements and the evolving plant design.
  • Cost, safety and risk management
    1. Identify and manage design risks, developing effective risk-reduction strategies and action plans.
    2. Identify applicable standards, regulations and codes, and ensure that these are considered throughout the design process. 
    3. Participate in hazard, safety and accident analyses, including hazard identification (HAZID) and hazard and operability (HAZOP) studies, and contribute to the definition of safety functions and development of the safety case.
    4. Contribute to capital and operational expenditure (CAPEX/OPEX) estimates.
  • Design development and delivery
    1. Develop design documentation and specifications, including contributions to the Basis of Design and design philosophies.
    2. Document design studies, verification and assessment activities, engineering assumptions and design decisions.
    3. Support the design development, procurement and testing of prototypes for key components, in collaboration with technology developers, suppliers and research partners.
    4. Provide engineering support for R&D activities conducted in-house and with external partners and collaborators.
  • Project coordination and collaboration
    1. Lead specific technical tasks or work packages assigned by the Head of TFC, in line with experience and expertise.
    2. Take ownership of specific subsystems throughout the pre-FEED and FEED studies, as assigned by the Head of TFC, in line with experience and expertise.
    3. Participate in technical meetings with partners, suppliers, research institutions and other collaborators.
    4. Collaborate closely with other engineering disciplines and contribute to the integration of TFC systems within the wider fusion plant.
    5. As required, undertake other relevant duties in support of project objectives.
  • GID-170 delivery (in the 2030s)
    1. Support the procurement and installation activities of the GID-170 TFC facilities.
    2. Develop commissioning plans and operating instructions.
The balance between process design, systems engineering, and process modelling and simulation will depend on each candidate’s background and area of expertise. All engineers are expected to work collaboratively across these areas, ensuring that modelling activities inform engineering decisions and that process design is supported by robust analysis.


Qualification and educational requirements

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in chemical engineering, process engineering, nuclear engineering, or a closely related discipline*. 

*In the case of a closely related discipline, the degree should be supported by relevant chemical engineering experience.

  • A minimum of 3 years design experience working as a Process Engineer in an industrial environment.

    Additional desirable qualifications relevant to process modelling and simulation:
  • A PhD or EngD in Chemical or Process Engineering or a closely related field.


Competences and preferred skills

1. Common skills

Essential

All applicants should demonstrate:

  • In-depth knowledge of chemical engineering principles, including thermodynamics, heat and mass transfer, process dynamics, and relevant transport phenomena.
  • Experience in the development of industrial-scale process engineering installations in complex environments requiring regulatory approval (ideally nuclear projects or similar).
  • Experience in the development of processes involving different fluids and conditions (cryogenic, vacuum, atmospheric pressure gas, high-pressure gas (up to 100 bara), liquid, etc.).
  • Experience in the design and development of integrated treatment unit operations (purification, separation, conditioning, etc.), ideally in the gas phase, and in the hydrogen or nuclear sectors.
  • Proficiency in at least one established process simulation tool, such as Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, UniSim, gPROMS, ProMax, CHEMCAD or equivalent.
  • Experience in requirements capture, documentation and management.
  • Experience working alongside multiple other engineering disciplines, such as mechanical, electrical, control, thermal and nuclear engineers.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams of engineers, technologists and physicists.
  • A proactive and self-motivated approach, with strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills.
  • Professional working proficiency in English. 

Desirable

All applicants would benefit from demonstrating:

  • Knowledge of tritium fuel cycle technologies and/or hydrogen isotope separation. Hands-on experience working with tritium would be an advantage.
  • Experience with the design or analysis of pumping technologies, heat exchangers or other key process equipment.
  • Familiarity with magnetic fusion systems and/or nuclear power plant systems.
  • Familiarity with environmental, nuclear safety and other relevant regulatory requirements. 
  • Knowledge of systems engineering and an understanding of configuration management and risk management.
  • Understanding of equipment qualification, manufacture, testing, inspection and pragmatic usability.
  • Knowledge of German or other European languages.

2. Specialist Skills

Candidates are expected to demonstrate strengths in one or more of the following areas, depending on their background and specialisation.

Process design and systems engineering

  • Experience in developing process architectures, heat and mass balances, PFDs and P&IDs, and in supporting equipment selection, sizing and integration.
  • Experience in developing Basis of Design (BoD) documentation, design philosophies, specifications, design descriptions and justifications.
  • Ability to assess alternative process technologies and configurations, considering performance, safety, technical maturity and operational requirements.
  • Experience in translating system requirements and process analysis into engineering specifications and design decisions.
  • Familiarity with process safety codes, standards and regulations, as well as safety-by-design principles, including the ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) approach.
  • Experience in engaging with potential technology suppliers and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs).

Process modelling and simulation

  • Proficiency in process modelling tools such as Aspen Custom Modeler, gPROMS custom modelling or equivalent.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming or scientific computing language, such as Python, Julia, MATLAB, Octave or C++.
  • Strong understanding of numerical methods applied to chemical engineering, including ordinary and partial differential equations (ODEs and PDEs), differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), discretisation techniques and numerical convergence.
  • Knowledge of numerical optimisation methods and their implementation, with the ability to apply them to process analysis and design optimisation.
  • Experience developing custom process models, integrating subsystem models or analysing dynamic process behaviour, along with model automation and analysis, to assess system performance, compare design options and support process optimisation is an advantage.


We are recruiting engineers with complementary technical strengths. Applicants who meet the common essential criteria and have relevant capability in one specialist profile are encouraged to apply; experience in every technology or software package listed is not expected.


The balance of responsibilities and the level of technical ownership will be agreed according to each successful candidate’s experience and the needs of the programme, with opportunities for candidates to grow and develop into greater technical ownership.

title: Product Frontend Engineer
description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account. The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components. The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device. Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native. The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished. Where design ends, engineering begins. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you. Requirements Who we are looking for You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed. You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building. You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels. You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does. Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works. The Team We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action. This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally. Familiarity with modern software development, testing, CI/CD, and release management practices. MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. title: VP Embedded Finance & Strategic Partnerships (m/w/d) 80-100%
description: Jobbeschreibung Mach mit uns Schweizer Kleinunternehmen noch erfolgreicher! Klingt nach einer grossen Vision? Genau das treibt uns jeden Tag an. Wir bei bexio leben die Philosophie, dass erstklassige, effiziente und smarte Softwarelösungen für jedes KMU zugänglich und erschwinglich sein müssen. Mit dieser Mission sind wir heute die führende Anbieterin für webbasierte Business-Software in der Schweiz. Unser Expansionskurs geht steil nach oben: Über 100'000 zufriedene Kunden, mehr als 7'000 Treuhand-Partner und ein starkes Team von über 150 motivierten Mitarbeitenden sprechen für sich. Um diese Erfolgsgeschichte weiterzuschreiben, suchen wir tatkräftige Unterstützung. Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel! Als VP Embedded Finance & Strategic Partnerships übernimmst du die unternehmerische Gesamtverantwortung für den Aufbau, die Skalierung und den langfristigen Erfolg eines zentralen neuen strategischen Wachstumspfeilers bei bexio. In direkter Berichtslinie zum CEO konzipierst, steuerst und implementierst du innovative Embedded-Finance-Lösungen innerhalb des bexio-Ökosystems. Dein Ziel ist es, unseren Schweizer KMU-Kunden und Treuhändern nahtlose, hochintegrierte Finanzdienstleistungen direkt aus der ERP-Software heraus bereitzustellen. Dabei verantwortest du das gesamte Partner- und In-Life-Management mit unserem Banking-Partner, stellst eine saubere regulatorische Abgrenzung (FINMA/Compliance) sicher und schaffst ein erstklassiges, automatisiertes Nutzererlebnis mit nachhaltigen Produkterlösen. Stellenanforderungen Was du bei uns bewegst Du definierst die Vision sowie die Go-to-Market- und Skalierungsstrategie für Embedded Finance und setzt diese in enger Abstimmung mit dem CEO, der Geschäftsleitung sowie Product und Tech um. Als Hauptansprechpartner und Verhandlungsführer gegenüber unserer Partnerbank steuerst du Vertragsgestaltungen, Revenue-Share-Modelle, SLAs, kommerzielle Rahmenbedingungen sowie die technische Schnittstellenkoordination. In enger Zusammenarbeit mit den internen Produkt- und Entwicklungsteams sorgst du für die intuitive Einbettung von Bankfunktionen in bestehende bexio-Workflows (z. B. Rechnungsstellung, Zahlungsverkehr, Liquiditätsmanagement). Nach dem Launch überwachst du kontinuierlich Performance (Sales, Support), Systemstabilität und Kundenzufriedenheit. Auf Basis von KPIs optimierst du Funnel- sowie Nutzungsraten und erweiterst das Produktportfolio laufend. Du stellst sicher, dass sämtliche bankenrelevanten und aufsichtsrechtlichen Pflichten (FINMA, GwG, KYC/AML, Bankgeheimnis, Meldewesen) vertraglich und operativ vollumfänglich durch den Bankpartner abgedeckt sind, während bei bexio höchste Datenschutz- und Datensicherheitsstandards (revDSG/DSGVO) eingehalten werden. Du startest als hochgradig strategische Lead-Funktion mit starker fachlicher Führung interdisziplinärer Projekt- und Produktteams (Sales, Support, Customer Success, Marketing, Finance) und baust im Zuge der Skalierung perspektivisch ein eigenes Team auf. Dein Rucksack für diese Stelle Abgeschlossenes Studium (Master/Bachelor) in Betriebswirtschaft, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Finance, FinTech oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation. Mindestens 7–10 Jahre relevante Berufs- und Führungserfahrung im FinTech-, Banking-as-a-Service- (BaaS) oder Bankenumfeld bzw. in stark wachsenden B2B-SaaS- oder Plattform-Unternehmen. Nachweisbare Erfolge in der Konzeption, Markteinführung und Skalierung komplexer Banken- oder Embedded-Finance-Integrationen sowie ausgewiesene Erfahrung in der Verhandlung strategischer Partnerschaften auf Executive-Ebene. Tiefes Verständnis von Embedded Finance, BaaS, Open Banking / API-Architekturen und B2B-Finanzdienstleistungen für KMU. Fundierte Kenntnisse der Schweizer Banken- und Finanzmarktregulatorik (FINMA, GwG, revDSG/DSGVO). Ausgeprägte Kompetenz in agiler Produktentwicklung (Scrum/SAFe), Schnittstellendesign und Portfoliomanagement. Starke analytische Fähigkeiten in Business-Case-Modellierung, Unit-Economics-Berechnung und KPI-gestütztem Management. Du bist ein verhandlungsstarker Strategietreiber mit hoher «technischer Übersetzungskompetenz» – du schlägst mühelos die Brücke zwischen Banken-Systemarchitekten, internen Tech-Teams und dem C-Level. Zudem zeichnest du dich durch ausgeprägtes Risikobewusstsein und Skalierungs-Mindset aus. Verhandlungssichere Kenntnisse (C1/C2 bzw. Muttersprache) in Deutsch, Französisch und Englisch. Darauf kannst du dich freuen Hybrid-Modell und Arbeitszeiten, die sich deinem Leben anpassen. 5 Wochen Ferien plus Option auf unbezahlten Urlaub. Yoga, Bootcamps, Massagen und legendäre Grill-Sessions. 16 Wochen Mutterschafts- und 3 Wochen Vaterschaftsurlaub. bexio übernimmt 63 % deiner Pensionskassenbeiträge – für mehr Netto vom Lohn. title: Senior SEO & GEO Manager
description: Who we are We believe travel can create Citizens of the World. When people cross Europe slowly, by train, they come back more curious, more open and better able to understand people unlike themselves.   With colleagues from more than 50 countries, our diversity sparks curiosity, insight and a culture of openness, which is essential to understanding our travellers and one another.   Three values connect everyone at Interrail: we lead with our purpose, we own our impact, and we choose for growth.   We work in a hybrid way, from our office in Utrecht and our homes across the Netherlands.   Who we’re looking for Someone who can shape how travellers discover Interrail, whether they’re typing into a search engine or asking an AI assistant to plan their trip. Exploring Europe by rail is one of the most transformative ways to travel, and there’s a big, untapped opportunity to make it even easier. With SEO and GEO, you’ll help travellers get inspired, plan and book their next rail adventure with an Interrail Pass in fewer steps.   Also, it’s good to know that the team has agreed to meet in the office every Tuesday and Thursday, so you’ll be expected to be in the office on these days to work side by side with your colleagues.   What you’ll be doing You’ll be joining the Growth team (in a nutshell: the people who turn traveller curiosity into journeys booked), reporting to our E-Commerce Lead.   You’ll own the end-to-end SEO and GEO strategy, so that Interrail is found, cited and recommended wherever travellers research rail travel in Europe. Working across content, product, engineering and PR/brand, you’ll turn search and AI visibility insight into meaningful, measurable growth.   Strategy and leadership Own and scale a unified SEO and GEO strategy and roadmap, aligned to commercial goals across our priority markets. Prioritise investment across markets and languages based on search demand, commercial opportunity and local traveller needs. Be our internal expert on how AI is changing travel discovery, embedding SEO and GEO thinking across marketing, content, PR/brand and product. Partner with engineering, content and product to get the right work prioritised and shipped. Technical SEO and architecture Own technical SEO for our large, complex site and set the technical roadmap with product and content. Lead our SEO architecture: hreflang at scale, domain and subfolder strategy, and localisation quality across languages. Make sure search engines and AI systems can access and understand the site, with the right structured data and clear, consistent information on passes, pricing and eligibility. Own our crawler access policy for AI bots together with legal and engineering, balancing visibility against content protection. GEO Own our GEO strategy and roadmap: how we earn mentions, citations and recommendations across markets and languages. Build our GEO measurement framework, tracking brand presence, citation share, share of voice against competitors and sentiment. Spot recurring inaccuracies in AI-generated answers, fix them at the source with the relevant teams and track whether accuracy improves. Partner with PR, partnerships and social to strengthen the off-site signals AI models rely on, from trusted travel publications to community presence and review platforms. Measure and attribute AI-referred traffic and conversions, and run structured tests to build repeatable GEO playbooks. Assess emerging opportunities, such as AI agents that plan and book travel, and advise on what Interrail needs to be ready. Content and topical authority Shape content strategy and topical authority across destinations, routes, guides and inspiration, balancing discovery with pass and booking intent. Make sure our content performs in both search results and AI answers, with clear factual structure and original rail expertise worth citing. Be the SEO and GEO advisor to the content team, building a shared roadmap that connects visibility opportunity to editorial output. Set and govern content quality standards (briefs, structure, internal linking, E-E-A-T) and upskill the team in SEO and GEO best practice. Identify gaps, cannibalisation and refresh opportunities, and advise on what to create, update, consolidate or retire. Measurement and reporting Forecast organic and AI-driven performance, set KPIs across both, and report clearly to senior stakeholders. What success looks like Non-brand searches make up a growing share of organic traffic and revenue across our priority markets. A GEO measurement framework is live, and our citation share and share of voice in AI answers are improving against key competitors. The SEO and GEO roadmap is agreed with product, engineering and content and delivered as planned, including website and CMS changes that launch without loss of organic visibility. Recurring inaccuracies about passes, pricing and eligibility in AI answers are identified, fixed at the source and measurably reduced. What we’re looking for Here’s what will help you in this role. If you don’t match every point, we’d still love to hear from you.   In terms of your experience and skills: Demonstrated experience leading SEO strategy across content and technical, ideally in travel, e-commerce or a large content or marketplace environment. Hands-on GEO experience, with examples of your approach, results, measurement limitations and the decisions that followed. A working understanding of how AI search experiences select and cite sources, and how that differs from traditional ranking. A strong track record in international and multilingual SEO at scale. raw.title: Senior SEO & GEO Manager
raw.description:
Who we are

We believe travel can create Citizens of the World. When people cross Europe slowly, by train, they come back more curious, more open and better able to understand people unlike themselves.

 

With colleagues from more than 50 countries, our diversity sparks curiosity, insight and a culture of openness, which is essential to understanding our travellers and one another.

 

Three values connect everyone at Interrail: we lead with our purpose, we own our impact, and we choose for growth.

 

We work in a hybrid way, from our office in Utrecht and our homes across the Netherlands.

 

Who we’re looking for

Someone who can shape how travellers discover Interrail, whether they’re typing into a search engine or asking an AI assistant to plan their trip. Exploring Europe by rail is one of the most transformative ways to travel, and there’s a big, untapped opportunity to make it even easier. With SEO and GEO, you’ll help travellers get inspired, plan and book their next rail adventure with an Interrail Pass in fewer steps.

 

Also, it’s good to know that the team has agreed to meet in the office every Tuesday and Thursday, so you’ll be expected to be in the office on these days to work side by side with your colleagues.

 

What you’ll be doing

You’ll be joining the Growth team (in a nutshell: the people who turn traveller curiosity into journeys booked), reporting to our E-Commerce Lead.

 

You’ll own the end-to-end SEO and GEO strategy, so that Interrail is found, cited and recommended wherever travellers research rail travel in Europe. Working across content, product, engineering and PR/brand, you’ll turn search and AI visibility insight into meaningful, measurable growth.

 

Strategy and leadership

  • Own and scale a unified SEO and GEO strategy and roadmap, aligned to commercial goals across our priority markets.

  • Prioritise investment across markets and languages based on search demand, commercial opportunity and local traveller needs.

  • Be our internal expert on how AI is changing travel discovery, embedding SEO and GEO thinking across marketing, content, PR/brand and product.

  • Partner with engineering, content and product to get the right work prioritised and shipped.

Technical SEO and architecture

  • Own technical SEO for our large, complex site and set the technical roadmap with product and content.

  • Lead our SEO architecture: hreflang at scale, domain and subfolder strategy, and localisation quality across languages.

  • Make sure search engines and AI systems can access and understand the site, with the right structured data and clear, consistent information on passes, pricing and eligibility.

  • Own our crawler access policy for AI bots together with legal and engineering, balancing visibility against content protection.

GEO

  • Own our GEO strategy and roadmap: how we earn mentions, citations and recommendations across markets and languages.

  • Build our GEO measurement framework, tracking brand presence, citation share, share of voice against competitors and sentiment.

  • Spot recurring inaccuracies in AI-generated answers, fix them at the source with the relevant teams and track whether accuracy improves.

  • Partner with PR, partnerships and social to strengthen the off-site signals AI models rely on, from trusted travel publications to community presence and review platforms.

  • Measure and attribute AI-referred traffic and conversions, and run structured tests to build repeatable GEO playbooks.

  • Assess emerging opportunities, such as AI agents that plan and book travel, and advise on what Interrail needs to be ready.

Content and topical authority

  • Shape content strategy and topical authority across destinations, routes, guides and inspiration, balancing discovery with pass and booking intent.

  • Make sure our content performs in both search results and AI answers, with clear factual structure and original rail expertise worth citing.

  • Be the SEO and GEO advisor to the content team, building a shared roadmap that connects visibility opportunity to editorial output.

  • Set and govern content quality standards (briefs, structure, internal linking, E-E-A-T) and upskill the team in SEO and GEO best practice.

  • Identify gaps, cannibalisation and refresh opportunities, and advise on what to create, update, consolidate or retire.

Measurement and reporting

  • Forecast organic and AI-driven performance, set KPIs across both, and report clearly to senior stakeholders.

What success looks like

  • Non-brand searches make up a growing share of organic traffic and revenue across our priority markets.

  • A GEO measurement framework is live, and our citation share and share of voice in AI answers are improving against key competitors.

  • The SEO and GEO roadmap is agreed with product, engineering and content and delivered as planned, including website and CMS changes that launch without loss of organic visibility.

  • Recurring inaccuracies about passes, pricing and eligibility in AI answers are identified, fixed at the source and measurably reduced.

What we’re looking for

Here’s what will help you in this role. If you don’t match every point, we’d still love to hear from you.

 

In terms of your experience and skills:

  • Demonstrated experience leading SEO strategy across content and technical, ideally in travel, e-commerce or a large content or marketplace environment.

  • Hands-on GEO experience, with examples of your approach, results, measurement limitations and the decisions that followed.

  • A working understanding of how AI search experiences select and cite sources, and how that differs from traditional ranking.

  • A strong track record in international and multilingual SEO at scale.

  • A solid technical foundation, including structured data, and the ability to influence engineering roadmaps.

  • Outstanding cross-functional collaboration: you align teams around a shared roadmap and take initiatives from idea to launch without direct authority, reviewing results together and applying the learnings.

  • A data-driven, commercial mindset: comfortable forecasting, sizing opportunity, attributing impact in a maturing channel and presenting to leadership.

  • A test-and-learn mindset, comfortable building new capabilities in a fast-changing environment.

  • Experience partnering closely with content, editorial, PR or brand teams.

  • Fluency with the core toolset: Google Search Console, GA4, an SEO platform such as Semrush or Ahrefs, a crawler such as Screaming Frog, log-analysis tools and GEO tracking tools.

  • Fluent English; another European language, ideally German, French, Italian or Spanish, is beneficial to have.

Our offer

  • A hybrid way of working, with some days each week in our Utrecht office and the rest from home.

  • A free NS train card, so you can travel across the Netherlands for work and in your free time.

  • A free Interrail Pass every year for you and a companion, so you can travel across Europe the way our travellers do.

  • Unlimited access to OpenUp, an online wellbeing platform.

  • A personal wellbeing allowance of up to €1,500.

  • A training allowance of up to €4,000 for learning that’s relevant to your role.

  • A variable annual bonus (target 4%), based on company and individual performance.

  • An annual team trip across Europe, so you see first-hand what our travellers experience.

  • The option to work from abroad for 20 days a year.

  • An annual leave package of 28 days, plus study days, volunteer days and a culture day.

  • Salary Scale: 60. Monthly gross salary (excluding 8% holiday allowance): €5,300 – €6,400 (full-time), based on experience.

Curious to apply?

Apply directly through our careers page.

 

  • We’ll ask you to share your CV in English (our business language) and tell us why you’re interested in Interrail and this role. It doesn’t hurt to be creative; we enjoy seeing your personality shine through.

  • For some roles, we may also ask you to complete a short task based on the real job, so you can show us your skills in practice.

 

If we’d like to get to know you better, the next step is a first conversation with Talent Acquisition, followed by interviews with the team. It’s a two-way conversation: a chance for you to explore Interrail, and for us to get to know you.

 

To keep our hiring fair, we use blind screening in the early stages. Your name, photo, date of birth, gender, nationality, contact details and social media links are hidden, so our first decisions are based only on your skills, experience and potential.

 

In the meantime

If you’re curious, why not check us out on LinkedIn and get a sense of our culture and values?

 

Got questions? Our team would be happy to help: just drop us a note at

 

While you’re here, you can plan your own trip and find your Pass at www.interrail.com.

Vind je het leuk om video's te maken en te editen, nieuwe ideeën te bedenken en content te creëren die écht opvalt? Dan zoeken wij jou! Bij BERG krijg je de ruimte om jouw creativiteit volop in te zetten. Je draait echt mee in ons team en krijgt de vrijheid om zelf ideeën aan te dragen, content te maken en projecten op te pakken. Geen stage waarbij je alleen meekijkt, maar een plek waar je zelf aan de slag gaat, veel leert en jouw ideeën werkelijkheid ziet worden. Samen maken we er een creatieve en vooral leuke stage van! Create your  FUTURE Als stagiair(e) Multi Media Design word jij onderdeel van ons creatieve Social Media team binnen de Branding afdeling. Je krijgt de ruimte om jouw creativiteit te laten zien en werkt mee aan allerlei gave projecten. Van social media content tot 360 campagnes: jij helpt mee om BERG op een creatieve manier onder de aandacht te brengen.   Wat ga je zoal doen? ·         Je bedenkt, ontwerpt en maakt toffe content voor onze social media kanalen. ·         Je gaat aan de slag met videomontage en grafisch ontwerp, van pakkende reels tot opvallende visuals. ·         Je helpt onze social media kanalen dagelijks up-to-date te houden. ·         Je ondersteunt bij influencer samenwerkingen en denkt mee over creatieve mogelijkheden. ·         Je werkt samen met ons creatieve team aan video- en designprojecten. ·         Je helpt mee aan onze 360 graden campagnes en krijgt een kijkje achter de schermen bij verschillende marketingactiviteiten.   En het leukste? Er is volop ruimte voor jouw eigen ideeën en creatieve input! Zie jij een trend voorbijkomen die perfect bij BERG past? Of heb je een origineel idee voor een video? Laat maar zien! 100%  YOU Jij bent iemand die niet alleen graag creatief bezig is, maar ook niet bang is om initiatief te nemen. Je hebt gevoel voor design, weet wat er speelt op social media en krijgt energie van het maken van content die echt opvalt. Je vindt het leuk om samen te werken, maar kunt ook prima zelfstandig aan de slag. Je schakelt makkelijk tussen verschillende projecten, denkt graag mee en houdt ervan om nieuwe dingen te leren. Daarnaast ben jij een enthousiaste tweede- of derdejaars hbo-student Communication & Multimedia Design (of een vergelijkbare opleiding). Herken jij jezelf hierin? Dan zijn we op zoek naar jou! Je hebt gevoel voor grafisch design en maakt graag opvallende content. Je hebt ervaring met Adobe Creative Cloud (o.a. Premiere Pro, After Effects, Photoshop en Illustrator). Je volgt de nieuwste trends op het gebied van social media, design en AI. Je werkt nauwkeurig, hebt oog voor detail en kunt goed omgaan met deadlines. Je spreekt en schrijft goed Nederlands en Engels. Je hebt een portfolio met werk waar je trots op bent! Je hoeft natuurlijk nog niet alles te kunnen. Je komt tenslotte bij ons om te leren! raw.description:
Finance Controller

Location: Netherlands

Start date: Q1 2027

Compensation: €70k - €80k annually (depending on experience)

Employment type: Full-time (contractor if outside Netherlands)

About DTACT

DTACT (Data Transform Act) is a data technology company that helps organizations transform complex information into clear, actionable insights. Founded in 2016, we work with government agencies and enterprises across Europe to solve critical data challenges and support better decision-making in areas such as cybersecurity, defense, intelligence, public safety, and critical infrastructure. Built on deep expertise in these domains, we develop innovative solutions that help organizations gain greater visibility, understanding, and control over their data.

As a fully remote and internationally distributed company, we combine technical excellence with a collaborative and adaptable way of working. Our mission is simple: to help organizations turn information into action, enabling faster, smarter decisions when they matter most.

The Role

We are looking for a Finance Controller to own DTACT’s finance function end-to-end as we continue to scale internationally. Reporting into the COO, you’ll take full ownership of accounting, collections, financial analytics, budgeting, and compliance (including our Dutch statutory obligations) — acting as the single point of accountability for finance in the business today. This is a hands-on, mid-level role: you’ll be expected to run the entire finance function largely on your own in the near term, while also bringing the leadership mindset and ambition to grow the function — and your own role — as DTACT expands.

What you'll do

  • Own end-to-end accounting operations — AP/AR, general ledger, and month end/year-end close — ensuring accurate, timely financial reporting.

  • Manage the full collections process: invoicing, aging follow-up, and cash flow forecasting.

  • Build and maintain finance analytics (dashboards, reports) that give leadership clear, real-time visibility into company performance.

  • Own the budgeting and forecasting cycle, partnering with department leads to track actuals against plan.

  • Ensure full compliance with Dutch tax and statutory reporting requirements (VAT, annual accounts) and manage relationships with external accountants, auditors, banks, and tax advisors.

  • Partner with People Operations on payroll processing and accuracy across jurisdictions, and own administration of the employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP).

  • Build and continuously improve finance processes, technical efficiencies and controls, laying the groundwork as the company grows.

What you'll bring

  • 5–8 years of progressive finance/accounting experience, including hands-on ownership of a full finance function — ideally within tech in a startup or scale-up environment.

  • Solid knowledge of Dutch accounting standards, tax regulations, statutory compliance requirements and payroll.

  • Proven ability to independently manage accounting, collections, budgeting, and financial analytics without a large supporting team.

  • Strong analytical skills and financial modeling ability; comfortable turning data into clear, actionable insights.

  • Leadership potential and genuine ambition to grow into a finance leadership role as the team and company scale.

  • A hands-on, “roll up your sleeves” attitude, paired with the ability to think and plan strategically.

  • Excellent communication skills in English and Dutch.

What's in for you

  • Competitive compensation and equity participation, including an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP), allowing you to share in DTACT's long-term success.

  • Remote-first flexibility, with the opportunity to work from anywhere within compatible time zones and a schedule that supports both collaboration and personal needs.

  • A trust-based culture built around asynchronous communication, empowering people to work independently while staying connected and aligned across teams.

  • Generous time off, including vacation days and local public holidays to help you rest, recharge, and maintain a healthy work-life balance.

  • Home office support, including high-quality equipment and a budget to create a productive and comfortable workspace.

  • An international and diverse team, where English is our company language and collaboration spans multiple countries, backgrounds, and perspectives.

  • High-impact work: DTACT helps organizations in and outside the government with mitigating their vulnerabilities and providing alerts to incoming threats.

We believe diverse teams build better solutions.

DTACT welcomes applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of background or identity. We hire based on skills, experience, and potential, and encourage everyone who meets the role requirements to apply.

Please note: Visa sponsorship is not available for this role. Candidates must be authorized to work in their country of residence.

title: Legal Counsel
description: Position Overview Axelera AI is a fast-growing AI semiconductor company headquartered in Eindhoven, building high-performance, energy-efficient AI acceleration hardware and software, from the Metis AI platform for edge inference to next-generation AI processing units. We are scaling quickly: new customers, new partners, new markets, and a growing volume of complex commercial deals across the global semiconductor supply chain. We are looking for an experienced commercial lawyer to be the engine of our commercial legal function. You will close deals, build the playbooks and processes that let the business move fast without taking on unmanaged risk, and lead how legal operates day to day, with AI in the loop so a lean team delivers more with less. This is a hands-on role with real scope to shape the function as it grows. Key responsibilities: Commercial contracting Draft, review and negotiate a high volume of commercial agreements: customer, distribution, reseller and OEM/ODM agreements; sales terms and EULAs; supply and manufacturing agreements (foundry, OSAT, component suppliers); technology and IP licences; software and SaaS agreements; evaluation, early access and development agreements; R&D collaboration and consortium agreements; services and vendor agreements; and MOUs, LOIs and partnership terms. Act as the trusted, pragmatic adviser to Sales, Product, Engineering, Operations and Finance, giving clear, commercial risk calls at pace. Advise on key semiconductor and AI issues: IP ownership and licensing, warranties and liability caps, product liability, export controls and sanctions, data protection and the EU AI Act. Support the CFO and Head of Legal on strategic matters, including corporate transactions and board-level work, as needed. Playbooks and scale Build AI-ready contract playbooks, fallback positions and approval matrices so AI tools and the business can handle routine deals with minimal Legal involvement. Create and own a library of standard templates for our core agreement types (e.g. NDA, customer terms, evaluation, distributor, supplier) aligned to our risk appetite. Train commercial teams on contract basics, negotiation positions and when to escalate to Legal. Legal operations Lead legal operations: intake and triage, prioritisation, SLAs and reporting on legal workload and turnaround. Own the legal tech and AI stack: select, implement and continuously improve AI review and drafting tools, CLM, e-signature and the contract repository, automating repeatable work end to end. Own contract lifecycle management, including obligation tracking, renewals and keeping contract records complete and up to date. Set up clear policies and processes that scale with the company. Collaboration Work alongside, supervise and mentor a Junior Legal Counsel, allocating work and reviewing output. Manage external counsel efficiently, including scope and budget, and determine which matters are best handled in-house. Report to the Head of Legal (in the interim, the CFO) and help shape the future structure of the legal team. Qualifications: Essential Qualified lawyer with 7+ years' PQE in commercial and corporate law, from a leading firm and/or in-house. Substantial in-house experience in tech, semiconductors, hardware or deep tech, ideally at a scale-up. A strong track record negotiating complex, high-value international contracts, including IP-heavy and supply chain deals. Hands-on use of AI tools in daily legal work, plus experience building playbooks and processes that let a small team scale. Commercial judgement that finds the route to yes, and the ability to explain risk simply to senior stakeholders. Comfort with ambiguity, high volume and shifting priorities. Fluent business English, our working and contract language. Desirable Semiconductor, AI or embedded systems experience (foundry, licensing, OEM deals). Knowledge of export controls (EU dual-use, US EAR), sanctions and the EU AI Act. Experience implementing CLM or AI contract tools, prompting, or building no-code automations. Experience mentoring junior lawyers, or exposure to venture-backed companies and governance. Dutch or another European language. How We Work: AI-First Legal We're building a lean legal function, not scaling by headcount. AI handles first-pass review, redlining, drafting and research, while lawyers focus on judgement and negotiation. Routine work is self-serve through templates and AI-assisted workflows. We measure turnaround and outcomes, and we use AI responsibly, with human review and clear guardrails on confidentiality and accuracy. Location Hybrid, with 2 days per week in our Amsterdam or Eindhoven office. What we offer This is your chance to shape and be part of a dynamic, fast-growing, international organization. We offer an attractive compensation package, including a pension plan, extensive employee insurances and the option to get company shares. An open culture that supports creativity and continual innovation is awaiting you. Collaborative ownership and freedom with responsibility is characteristic for the way we act and work as a team. At Axelera AI, we wholeheartedly embrace equal opportunity and hold diversity in the highest regard. Our steadfast commitment is to cultivate a warm and inclusive environment that empowers and celebrates every member of our team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds to join us in shaping the future of AI. Axelera AI may at times work with external parties (such as recruiters, headhunters, or executive search firms) to support both publicly posted and confidential searches.   • Develop, implement, and maintain scalable data pipelines for batch and distributed data processing.
  • Optimise Spark workloads and Hadoop cluster performance, including resource allocation, job scheduling, and capacity management.
  • Work with PostgreSQL and other enterprise data systems to support data integration, storage, and processing requirements.
  • Support the deployment and management of containerised applications using Kubernetes and Helm.
  • Implement and manage service-to-service communication and traffic management using Istio Service Mesh.
  • Ensure software dependencies, container images, packages, and platform components can be deployed and maintained without external internet connectivity.
  • Implement secure configuration and operational practices aligned with enterprise security requirements.
  • Troubleshoot complex infrastructure, cluster, application, and data pipeline issues.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure, security, DevOps, and application teams to ensure platform stability and availability.
  • Maintain technical documentation, deployment procedures, operational runbooks, and platform architecture documentation.
  • Support integration with legacy enterprise data systems, including VSAM.

  • Strong hands-on experience deploying, configuring, and administering Apache Hadoop clusters.

Preferred / Desirable Skills

  • Familiarity with Linux system administration.
  • Experience with infrastructure automation and configuration management.
  • Knowledge of data security, access controls, encryption, and secure data handling.
  • Experience with monitoring, logging, and platform observability.
  • Exposure to DevOps and CI/CD practices in restricted-network environments.
